standard.title: Local First Nations interconnections
standard.description: the interconnections of First Nations Australians to a local Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFK04): Students identified the importance of Country/Place to First Nations Australians and named the local language group. From Y1 (AC9HS1K03): Students explored place features including through Dreaming and Creation stories.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the interconnections of First Nations Australians to a local Country/Place.

nodes.label: Language, Country/Place and spirituality
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the relationship between language, Country/Place and spiritual identity for the local First Nations Australian language group.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one connection between the local First Nations Australian language group and Country/Place using a provided source.
nodes.typical_width: Liaise with community to identify the local language group; explore the relationship between language, Country/Place and spirituality for that group; listen to stories connecting local First Nations Australians with land, sea, waterways, sky and animals.
wider: Investigate why language is central to Country/Place connection and what is lost when language is not maintained
Compare the local language group's connections to Country/Place with those of another First Nations group from a different region
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding the language-Country/Place-spirituality nexus is needed before students can explain interconnections meaningfully — without this, acknowledgement practices become procedural rather than understood.

response_modes.reason: The three-way relationship between language, Country and spirituality is conceptually dense for Year 2 — use community voices and concrete local examples to anchor the concept.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Direct community engagement at this node provides irreplaceable authentic connection — this is one of the richest widening opportunities in the Year 2 curriculum.
success_criteria: Describes at least one connection the local First Nations language group has to Country/Place
Uses the name of the local First Nations language group correctly

nodes.label: Acknowledgement of Country and Welcome to Country
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain when Acknowledgement of Country and Welcome to Country are used and why they respectfully recognise Country/Place, Traditional Owners and Custodians.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain the purpose of Acknowledgement of Country and Welcome to Country and when each is used.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss when to use Acknowledgement of Country and Welcome to Country at ceremonies and events; explain how these practices respectfully recognise the Country/Place and Traditional Owners and Custodians of the land, sea, waterways and sky.
wider: Write or participate in an Acknowledgement of Country for the school that reflects genuine understanding of the local Country/Place and language group
Explore how protocols around Acknowledgement of Country differ between communities and discuss why those differences exist

response_modes.reason: Acknowledgement and Welcome to Country practices integrate language, Country/Place and interconnection knowledge into a civic act — the integration of understanding into practice.

success_criteria: Explains the purpose of Acknowledgement of Country and Welcome to Country
Correctly states when each is used (Acknowledgement by anyone; Welcome by Traditional Owner)
